chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad and Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad al-Nakhaʿī, who said: Sufyān ibn Muḥammad al-Ḍubaʿī narrated to me, saying:
I wrote to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام asking him about al-walījah, and it is the saying of Allah, the Exalted:
“And they did not take, apart from Allah, nor His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, nor the believers, any walījah.”

I said to myself: “It is not in the Book—who do you think the believers are here?” Then the reply came back: “Al-walījah is the one who is set up apart from the Walī al-Amr. And your soul has spoken to you about who the believers are in this place; they are the Imams عليهم السلام who pledge security upon Allah, so He ratifies their guarantee.”

key_terms.أَمَانَهُمْ: their guarantee of safety or protection
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: the Imams عليهم السلام, identified as the intended referents in the verse
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the believers; here interpreted as the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.الْوَلِيجَةِ: an intimate associate or inner confidant taken as an alternative authority
key_terms.وَلِيِّ الْأَمْرِ: the holder of authority, the rightful divinely appointed guardian

ai.seo_question: Who are “the believers” mentioned in the verse about not taking a walījah besides Allah, His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and the believers?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic term al-walījah as someone taken in place of the rightful divinely appointed authority. It identifies “the believers” in this verse as the Imams عليهم السلام, presenting the verse as a proof-text connected to wilayah and religious authority in Shia interpretation.
